definition: In its primary use, keeping its own quantity, number, or ordinal meaning, the form heads a nominal with a separate determiner before it and no noun after it: the few, the many, the other two, the little that remains, %the both of us, the last twice, the some who. CGEL's fused modifier-head with a determinative (pp. 415-416); ordinary Head's determinative heading a nominal after a determiner. Excludes: uses that name a person, thing, kind, or version (a he, the real me, a special someone; see secondary_set_denoting_use); conversions with a different sense (somes, the Any field, the enough that defines me, totality the all of me); names, titles, slips, and correlative the (the more the merrier).
applies_to: all 138 forms except the NA set
na_policy: NA = the form never heads a nominal. Determinatives coded n in 2021 on both functions_as_fused_determiner_head and functions_as_head_of_partitive_construction (a, a_certain, many_a, last, next, no, such, the, us_det, we_det, you_det, what_det, whatever_det, which_rel_det, whichever_rel_det), plus the dependent genitive pronouns (my, your_sing, your_plur, her_dep, its, our, their_sing, their_plur, one_s). every is not NA (CGEL p. 416 excludes it explicitly; it has marginal head uses). his, whose_int, whose_rel, whoever_s, whosever, whosoever_s are not NA (they can stand alone). NA never means "not looked at".
evidence_summary: Sourced for most forms: pronouns n from CGEL p. 429 (pronouns "do not permit determiners"); cardinals, few, many, little y (CGEL pp. 393, 416; records); every, various, much, enough, sufficient, compounds n (CGEL pp. 393, 397, 416, 423); once n, any n (records); both, some, all, twice marginal (CGEL p. 377; records). CGEL's licence (p. 415) is a default, not a condition: both and some head without a modifier use; every modifies without heading. 20 cells are Claude proposals or unsourced (14%).

definition: The form heads a nominal with an external determiner (article, cardinal, demonstrative, genitive) or plural -s, or both, in a use that denotes a person, thing, kind, or version fitting the description the form gives, without the form's primary quantificational, deictic, or person value: Is it a he or a she?, two mes, the real me, a new everything, a certain someone else, an anybody, nobodies. Counted whatever CGEL's category for it (CGEL calls he/she here common nouns, p. 429 n. 46, and a nobody a conversion, p. 423 n. 43). Excludes conversions with a different sense (somes "the religiously affiliated", label any, enough "sufficiency", totality all), uses that keep the quantity meaning (the few, the some who), names, titles, mentions, and slips. The criterion is semantic.
applies_to: all 138 forms except the NA set
